newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Easdaq says volume to mid-March totalled $113 mln.
newsitem.headline: Easdaq says volume to mid-March totalled $113 mln.

text.p: Europe's fledgling growth stocks market Easdaq, which is set to see its eighth listing next week, said on Wednesday market volume had totalled $113.1 million since trading kicked off last November.
Belgian biotechnology firm Innogenetics, which was the second to list on the Brussels-based pan-European exchange, accounted for $73.3 million.

Easdaq - the European Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations System - is modelled on New York's successful Nasdaq exchange, and has a market capitalisation of more than one billion dollars.
"I have read (comments) that Easdaq is not Nasdaq. I think Easdaq is Nasdaq, but not the Nasdaq of today," said Dirk Tirez, a member of Easdaq's market authority and head of memberships.
He was presenting Easdaq at a seminar about the Brussels stock exchange and new growth stocks markets, organised by Editions Laurence de Hemptinne.
Easdaq provides dual listing facilities for Nasdaq quoted stocks, as well as new listings via initial public share offers, and hopes to have 50 stocks quoted by the end of the year.
Tirez said an unofficial Easdaq all-share index which started at 100 points with the first listing on November 27 now stood at around 110 points.
It had dipped to about 96 in December, following a similar trend on Wall Street, before recovering to peak at 118 points around end-January/early February.
Easdaq has an upcoming rival in Euro.NM, a project involving the Paris, Amsterdam, Brussels and Frankfurt stock exchanges.
Each of the four bourses is developing a small capitalisation "New Market" - the Paris and Frankfurt markets are already up and running - which will be linked to up in a federation.

"What distinguishes Easdaq from the local New Markets is (higher) market capitalisation. We believe market capitalisation should be relatively high in order to get the necessary market liquidity," Tirez said.
